reviewer: Claude Code (agent self-review; not an independent review)
note: Candidate inventory only. It is not the approved registry: docs/organisation/skills.json is unchanged and still has no entries. 'state' is where a candidate is in review; 'recommendation' is the agent's proposal. Only an owner_approval record may move a candidate to approved, installed or revoked.

locations.shared-agents-skills: User-level shared skill folder installed by the Skills CLI. Claude Code reaches it through symlinks in its user skill folder.
locations.claude-user-skills: Claude Code user skill folder, holding real directories that are not symlinks.
locations.plugin:ecc@2.2.3: ECC Claude Code plugin, version 2.2.3, git commit d2ef268059.
locations.remote-connector: Hosted MCP connector. No local skill package to inspect.

hash_method: skill_md_sha256 is SHA-256 of SKILL.md. tree_sha256 is SHA-256 over sorted lines 'relative-path NUL file-sha256'. upstream_match compares SKILL.md with the source repository's default branch on 2026-11-23.

candidates.compatibility: Instructions only. disable-model-invocation is true, so the model cannot self-invoke it; it must be loaded explicitly.
candidates.rationale: Pure editing rules, no tools. Local copy differs from upstream, so pin one reviewed revision before approval.
Short failing-test-first bug workflow that explicitly allows skipping impractical tests and demands before/after evidence.

candidates.compatibility: Model-invocable. Examples are JavaScript, Jest and Playwright.
candidates.rationale: Duplicates tdd. Requires a checkpoint commit per stage and 80% coverage for every change, which is heavier than the engineering standard asks for.

candidates.compatibility: Model-invocable. Bundled hitl-loop.template.sh only prompts and reads terminal input; it makes no network calls.
candidates.rationale: Requires a reproducible red signal before hypotheses, redacts secrets, and removes debug logs before done.

candidates.compatibility: disable-model-invocation is true. Links to a Claude Code adapter document that the flat install does not include.
candidates.rationale: Matches KAREN's evidence rule: check the real artefact, not a proxy. Pin the current upstream revision and resolve the missing adapter link first.

candidates.compatibility: Model-invocable. Commands assume a Node project; the secret grep covers only .ts and .js files.
candidates.rationale: Its fixed npm phases do not fit Python projects such as KAREN OS, and its secret scan is weaker than scripts/check_pr.py. Project checks already cover this.

candidates.compatibility: disable-model-invocation is true. It reviews maintainability only, not correctness or security.
candidates.rationale: Strict structural review with clear blockers. Use it only for the substantial or high-impact profile that PR B defines, and pair it with a correctness and security review.

candidates.compatibility: Model-invocable. Expects a tracker configured by another skill; KAREN uses gh and the GitHub issue instead.
candidates.rationale: Separates standards findings from spec findings, which suits issue-based PRs. The spec source must be the GitHub issue, not the setup skill's tracker.

candidates.compatibility: Model-invocable checklist. Examples target Next.js, Supabase and Solana.
candidates.rationale: Useful OWASP-style checklist. Use it as a checklist only: 'npm audit fix' and 'npm update' change dependencies and need their own approval.

candidates.compatibility: Runs third-party code through unpinned npx. --fix rewrites agent configuration. --opus requires a paid API key.
candidates.rationale: Runs third-party code without a pinned version, can rewrite configuration, and can incur API spending. These need separate approval and conflict with zero default spend.

candidates.compatibility: Aimed at external bounty programmes and disclosure reports.
candidates.rationale: Targets other people's systems and builds working exploits. That needs a separately authorised security-testing engagement, not routine engineering.

candidates.compatibility: Model-invocable. Tells the agent to install globally with confirmation skipped.
candidates.rationale: Treats install counts and stars as trust and installs with -g -y. KAREN requires a full package review and owner approval before any install. Replace it with the PR D discovery procedure.

candidates.source: unknown: no lock entry, licence file or source link in either copy
candidates.compatibility: Hashes are for the Claude Code copy. The shared copy has a different, shorter SKILL.md (sha256 798785fa...); every other file is the same. Claude Code and other agents therefore load different instructions. Scripts import only standard-library modules and read bundled CSV data.
candidates.rationale: The content looks low-risk and states that it installs nothing. Hold until the source and licence are established and one copy is chosen.

candidates.source: unknown repository; frontmatter author claudekit, version 2.1.0
candidates.compatibility: Generator scripts load .env files from the skill folder and the agent's user configuration folders, then send prompts to Google Gemini.
candidates.rationale: Reads credentials from user configuration and sends data to an external paid model provider. That needs a sensitive-data destination and spending approval.

candidates.compatibility: shadcn_add.py runs npx to add components to a project.
candidates.rationale: Project-specific and stack-specific. Approve per project that uses shadcn, not as a company default.

candidates.compatibility: No local package and no lock entry under any name containing 'ponytail'.
candidates.rationale: Named in the charter as the required coding-stage skill, but nothing exists to review. The owner must supply its source.

candidates.source: Figma hosted MCP connector; it names a /figma-use skill
tools: Figma MCP tools, including write tools
candidates.compatibility: The connector is available in Claude Code. No local Figma plugin or figma-use skill package is installed, so there is nothing to hash.
candidates.rationale: Editable Figma design depends on the connector's write tools and account. Test it in a runtime and get owner approval of the connector scope first.
